hints.content:
The starting height of the red balloon corresponds to the value of $h$ when $t=0$. To find it, all we need is to substitute $\blue t=\blue 0$ into the formula for $h$:

$\begin{align} 
h&=\dfrac{1}{2}\blue t+4 \\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\blue 0+4 \\\\
&=\pink{4}
\end{align}$

This means that the red balloon started at a height of $\pink{4}$ meters.

The table of values for the blue balloon shows that for each decrease of $\blue{\text{time}}$ by $\blue 2$ seconds, $\pink{\text{height}}$ decreases by $\pink 1$ meter. We can extend the table according to this rate to find the value of $\pink{\text{height}}$ when $\blue{\text{time}}$ was $\blue 0$ seconds:  
  

[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the blue balloon started at a height of $\pink{3}$ meters.

**Since $\pink{4}>\pink{3}$, the red balloon started from a greater height.**

hints.content:
The rate at which the red balloon ascended is represented by the slope of the graph of $h = \dfrac{1}{2} t + 4$. Since the formula for $h$ is in *slope-intercept form*, we can determine that the slope is $\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}$. This means that the red balloon ascended at a rate of $\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}$ meters per second.

The rate at which the blue balloon ascended is the ratio of the corresponding differences in $\pink{\text{height}}$ and $\blue{\text{time}}$:

$\dfrac{\Delta \pink{\text{height}}}{\Delta \blue{\text{time}}}=\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

This means that the blue balloon ascended at a rate of $\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}$ meters per second.

**Since $\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}=\green{\dfrac{1}{2}}$, both balloons ascended at the same rate.**

Let's sum it up:

- The red balloon started from a greater height.

- Both balloons ascended at the same rate.

question.content:
Two hot-air balloons, one red and one blue, took off at the same time from different platforms. Each began ascending at a constant rate.

The following equation gives the height (in meters) of the red hot-air balloon as a function of time (in seconds).

$h = \dfrac{1}{2} t + 4$

The height (in meters) of the blue hot-air balloon as a function of time (in seconds) is given by the following table of values:

$\text{Time}$ (seconds) | $\text{Height}$ (meters)
:-: | :-:
$4$ | $5$
$6$ | $6$
$8$ | $7$

**Which balloon started at a greater height?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

**Which balloon ascended faster?**

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: They both started at the same height
They both ascended at the same rate
